newsitem.title: MOROCCO: French Accor group buys Moroccan hotels at $5.3 ml.
newsitem.headline: French Accor group buys Moroccan hotels at $5.3 ml.

text.p: French hotel Accor group on Tuesday bought the Moroccan three-star Moussafir hotel network located mainly in tourist cities at $5.3 million, Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj said.
Kabbaj told a news conference: "Accor group finalised on Tuesday an agreement with its Moroccan partners to purchase Moussafir hotel network at 50 million dirhams".
This was a "first tranche" of Accor's expected investments in the country, he added.

Moussafir company, which is owned by Morocco's largest private conglomerate ONA Group and state-owned railway firm Office National des Chemins de Fer (ONCF), has six hotels in tourists cities such as Marrakesk, Fez and Oujda.

The French group earlier said it plans to buy nine Moroccan hotels, including Moussafir, and invest more than $100 million to develop tourism and leisure facilities in Morocco's economic and financial capital of Casablanca.
Accor will take in charge management of hotel complexes in the southern cities of Marrakesh, Agadir, Zagora and Ouarzazate, it said.
The group will set up a Thalassotherapy unit in Essaouira, on the Atlantic coast, the ministry said.
Morocco expects up to $1.0 billion as foreign investments in 1997 against an estimated $450 million in 1996, the minister said.
